items.stem: x₁, …, xₙ is a random sample from f(x, θ) = θe^(−θx), θ > 0, x > 0.
statements: Σxᵢ/n is the maximum likelihood estimate of θ
Σxᵢ is the sufficient statistic for θ
Σxᵢ follows a Gamma distribution with parameter (1, θ)
items.explanation: B and C are true, D is false — ΣXᵢ ~ Gamma(n, θ), not Gamma(1, θ). A is false as written (the MLE of θ is n/Σxᵢ), so this item is flawed; the only option containing both B and C without D is (C). When a multi-statement question has no perfect option, eliminate on the statement you are surest about.

A.why: keyed true, though strictly the MLE of θ is n/Σxᵢ — a flaw in the question

B.why: unbiased and a function of the complete sufficient statistic

D.why: Gamma(n, θ); Gamma(1, θ) is a single exponential

items.stem: X₍₁₎ ≤ … ≤ X₍ᵣ₎ are the first r order statistics of a sample of size n from an exponential distribution with mean θ. With T₁ = (1/r)ΣX₍ᵢ₎ and T₂ = X₍ᵣ₎/r, which is unbiased for θ?
items.explanation: Type II censoring. The total time on test is ΣX₍ᵢ₎ + (n − r)X₍ᵣ₎, with expectation rθ, so dividing by r gives an unbiased estimator. Check it at r = n: the correction vanishes and it becomes X̄.

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ iid with pdf f(x|θ) = e^(−(x−θ)) for x ≥ θ.
statements: If Y = min(X₁,…,Xₙ) then f(y) = n·e^(−n(y−θ)), y ≥ θ
items.explanation: E(X) = θ + 1 and V(X) = 1, so A is true and D false. V(X̄) = 1/n, so C is false. The minimum of n exponentials is exponential at n times the rate, so B is true.

A.why: E(X) = θ + 1, so the WLLN gives this limit

B.why: the minimum of n exponentials has n times the rate

D.why: the limit is θ + 1, not θ

items.stem: h is an unbiased estimator of θ with E(h²) < ∞, and T is sufficient for Fθ. Which are TRUE?
statements: E(h|T) is the unique UMVUE of θ
items.explanation: A and B are Rao–Blackwell. D is true because sufficiency is exactly what makes E(h|T) free of θ. C is false — uniqueness as UMVUE needs completeness, which the question never assumes. That single missing word is the whole item.

D.why: sufficiency makes the conditional distribution free of θ

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ iid exponential with mean θ, T_S = ΣXᵢ, and T(x₁) = 1 if X₁ > x₀, else 0. Then E[T(X₁)|T_S] is the UMVUE of:
items.explanation: E[T(X₁)] = P(X₁ > x₀) = e^(−x₀/θ). Rao–Blackwell changes the estimator, never the estimand — so read E(h) first and the answer follows with no computation.

items.stem: X₁, …, Xₙ is a random sample from Poisson(λ), with X̄ the sample mean and S² the sample variance (divisor n − 1).
statements: X̄ + S² is unbiased for λ
items.explanation: Mean and variance both equal λ, so A and B hold. X̄ + S² has expectation 2λ, so C fails. Any weights summing to one preserve unbiasedness, so D holds for 0.3 and 0.7 or any other such pair.

B.why: for a Poisson the variance equals the mean
